content:
# Crew

Crew is a team work tracker with organizations, projects, issues and activity.

## Issues and discussion

Open a project's Issues page to filter work by text, workflow state, assignee, priority and label. Create or edit the full issue record: Markdown description, status, priority, assignee, fractional estimate, due date, parent and labels. Project numbers are sequential and never reused after deletion. Parent cycles and cross-project labels/statuses are rejected with field errors. Archived projects are read-only. Project label management supports names and colors, and updates issue views and search event snapshots.

Issue detail provides Markdown rendering, parent and child links, safe comment previews, a project-visible mention picker, author/admin comment edits, and blocks/duplicates/relates controls. Directed relations display their inverse meanings on the other issue; symmetric relates links cannot duplicate in reverse. Raw HTML is escaped and executable link schemes are inactive. Mentions resolve only to people who can read the project. Guests read and comment only on granted projects; issue changes require member access.

Use `crew issue help` for the full issue CLI. Typical commands are `issue create PROJECT --title TEXT`, `issue list PROJECT --label ID --query TEXT`, `issue edit ISSUE --estimate 3.5 --due 2028-02-29`, `issue comment ISSUE --body TEXT`, and `issue relate ISSUE --target ISSUE --kind blocks`. Nullable fields accept `none`; deletion requires `--yes`. Description/comment file inputs avoid shell quoting. [Issue API, event schema and CLI](docs/api-work-issues.md) documents every field, permission, pagination shape, mention form and relation meaning.

## Demo data

Run `npm run seed` to create the idempotent Crew Demo organization, Delivery team, DEMO project, three issues, and accounts `owner@crew.demo`, `member@crew.demo`, and `guest@crew.demo`. Each demo account uses password `crew-demo-password-2026`. These are local demonstration credentials; keep the data private. Re-running seed preserves existing demo project/issue edits and avoids duplicate records.

## Boards, sprints and files

Open a project’s Board to drag issues between or within ordered workflow columns. Every card also has a keyboard move menu; select several cards to edit status, assignee and labels atomically. Open Sprints to create a dated goal, preview scope additions, start one active sprint, review the daily points/issue-count burndown, and complete it with an explicit carry-over target. Historical sprint results remain fixed. Issue pages include streaming attachments with upload progress/cancel, the configured size limit, SHA-256 details, exact downloads and delete controls.

Use `crew board help` and `crew sprint help` for all board, bulk, planning and streaming file commands. `crew board attach ISSUE --file PATH` streams a file; `crew board download ATTACHMENT --output PATH` verifies size and SHA-256 while writing a new file. Runtime blobs are under `CREW_DATA_DIR/attachments`; back up them with crew.sqlite while the service is stopped. The protected API and CLI enforce the same role/project/token rules.

## Project planning

Open Projects to create an organization project, configure its key/name/description, and edit its ordered workflow. Status IDs remain stable during rename/reorder; move issues before removing an occupied status. Workflows require todo and done categories. Owners/admins manage projects; members collaborate; guests read only granted projects. Archive hides a project from the current-project list and protects issue edits; restore it from the archived list. Numbered project keys remain fixed so issue references stay meaningful.

Use `crew project create --org ID --key TEAM --name "Team roadmap"`, `project list`, `project show ID`, `project update ID --description TEXT`, `project archive ID`, `project restore ID`, `project workflow ID`, or `project workflow-set ID --file workflow.json`. Project deletion requires `project delete ID --yes`. See [Work API and CLI](docs/api-work.md) for request shapes, cursor lists, workflow files, permissions and lifecycle behavior.


## Setup

Use Node 22.23.1 and npm 10.9.8. Run `npm ci --fetch-retries=0 --fetch-timeout=60000 --no-audit --no-fund`, `npm run build`, `npm run prepare-tests`, and `npm test`. Start with `npm start` and open http://localhost:4100.

## Configuration

`PORT` defaults to 4100. `CREW_DATA_DIR` defaults to ./data and contains crew.sqlite plus attachment blobs. Set `CREW_SECRET`, `CREW_BASE_URL`, and `CREW_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (default 25 MiB). Back up the entire data folder while Crew is stopped. Keep it private. The diagnostic default secret must be replaced for deployment.

## Packages and scripts

shared holds validation, schemas and query logic; server owns HTTP/SQLite; web is Preact built with esbuild; cli is the `crew` executable. Each package has `npm test`; web also has `npm run build`. Root scripts are build, prepare-tests, test, start, seed and smoke. Tests run on temporary databases through actual HTTP.

## Authentication and CLI

Web sessions use httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies. Cookie mutations require X-Crew-Request: 1. `crew login --url URL --email EMAIL --password PASSWORD` stores a restricted config file. `crew whoami --json` reads it; `--config` chooses another file. Personal API tokens are supplied with --token or CREW_TOKEN. CREW_URL overrides the configured API URL.

## API and permissions

See [API](docs/api.md) and [architecture](docs/architecture.md). People supplies the common organization/project permission service, work emits changes, insight consumes them. Lists return items/nextCursor with limit 1–200.

## Filter language

The insight lane documents its boolean filter grammar and examples after integration.

## Known limitations

This is a diagnostic build, not a released service. No mail is sent: invitations, resets and digests live in the protected local outbox. Production TLS and external backups are operator concerns. No test skips are currently declared.

## Organizations and teams

Open Organizations to create a workspace, rename it, manage its roster and roles, and create teams. Owners and admins manage access; only owners manage other owners, and every organization must retain an owner. Members can collaborate across organization projects. Guests can read organization people and teams, and read/comment only in explicitly granted projects. Removing membership removes team access and project grants. Team membership does not grant access outside the organization. See [People API and permission service](docs/api-people.md) for endpoints, exact scopes, project access methods and the single local outbox schema. Invitations, session security, tokens and their CLI/admin controls are assigned to the next people milestone.

# Work planning API

All paths are prefixed with `/api/v1`. Sessions send `X-Crew-Request: 1` for mutations. Work uses the shared people permission service and domain event bus. See [issue, label and discussion endpoints](api-work-issues.md).

## Projects and workflows

`GET /projects` lists accessible projects, optionally `orgId`, `archived=true` or `archived=all`. `GET /orgs/:orgId/projects` lists one organization. Filtering happens before opaque cursor pagination (`limit` up to 200, `cursor`). Guests see only explicitly granted projects.

`POST /orgs/:orgId/projects` creates `{key,name,description?,statuses?}`. Keys are normalized uppercase, 2–12 letters/digits beginning with a letter, unique within an organization. The default ordered workflow is Todo (todo), Doing (active), Done (done). Owner/admin permission `project:manage` is required.

`GET /projects/:projectId` returns `{project,permissions}`. Projects expose stable id, orgId, key, name, description, archived, nextIssueNumber, createdAt, updatedAt and ordered statuses. Each status exposes id, projectId, name, category and position. `PATCH` accepts key/name/description/archived/statuses. A key is immutable once an issue has been numbered. Archive hides a project from the default list; restore with `{archived:false}`. `DELETE` removes the project and guest grants and emits its final event.

`GET /projects/:projectId/workflow` returns statuses. `PUT` accepts `{statuses:[{id?,name,category}]}` in desired order. Preserve existing IDs to rename/reorder statuses. New entries omit ID. Names must be unique, and at least one todo and one done category must remain. A status containing an issue cannot be removed; move those issues first. Workflow replacement is atomic.

Read requires `project:read`; project configuration requires owner/admin `project:manage`. Role access and token scopes both apply. Every mutation emits actorId/orgId/projectId/entityType/entityId/action/before/after/time.

## Boards and atomic bulk edits

`GET /projects/:projectId/board` returns the project and ordered columns `{status,issues}`. Query `q` and `assigneeId` filter cards. `POST /issues/:issueId/move` accepts `{statusId,beforeId?}` or `{statusId,afterId?}`. No anchor appends. Anchors must belong to the destination column. Ranks use fractional insertion, deterministic ID tie-breaking, and an atomic rebalance when precision is exhausted. Every move emits a full issue before/after event.

`POST /projects/:projectId/issues/bulk` accepts `{issueIds,changes:{statusId?,assigneeId?,labelIds?},addLabelIds?,removeLabelIds?}`. Null assignee clears assignment; labelIds replaces labels, add/remove edits preserve others. Replacement cannot be mixed with add/remove. Every referenced issue/status/assignee/label is validated before a single transaction applies all changes. Cross-project issues and invalid edits leave every selected issue unchanged. Each modified issue emits its complete event. Both actions require `issue:write` and reject archived projects.

The board at `#/projects/:projectId/board` supports native drag/drop, pointer drag, per-card keyboard move menus, search/assignee filters, and selected-card bulk status/assignee/label forms. Errors remain visible and refresh follows successful persistence.

## Sprints and burndown

`GET/POST /projects/:projectId/sprints` lists or creates `{name,goal?,startDate,endDate}`. Dates are real YYYY-MM-DD calendar dates, end on/after start, with at most 366 days in the planned interval. Lists accept status (`planned`, `active`, `completed`) and cursor pagination. Read requires `project:read`; planning mutations require `project:write`, with current role and token scope. Archived projects reject planning changes.

`GET /sprints/:sprintId` returns `{sprint,issues}`; `history=true` includes removed scope snapshots. `PATCH` updates metadata; active start dates are fixed. `DELETE` is allowed only while planned. `POST /sprints/:sprintId/start` activates a planned sprint; a project can have one active sprint. `POST /sprints/:sprintId/issues` accepts `{issueIds}`. `DELETE /sprints/:sprintId/issues/:issueId` removes scope. Scope changes are atomic, preserve their history, and reject cross-project, duplicate, or other unfinished-sprint assignments.

`POST /sprints/:sprintId/complete` accepts `{carryOverSprintId?}`. Only an active sprint completes. Carry-over targets another planned sprint in the same project and carries only unfinished issues. The result stores completedIssueIds, unfinishedIssueIds, completedPoints, remainingPoints, carriedIssueIds and carryOverSprintId. Completed metadata/scope totals are immutable even when live issues later change.

`GET /sprints/:sprintId/burndown` returns `{sprint,unit:'points',days,changes}`. Days contain date, scope, remaining, scopeIssues, remainingIssues, idealRemaining and future. Future actuals are null. Null estimates contribute zero points and still count as issues. Scope, estimate, completion, reopening and deletion events produce ledger deltas, so historical daily values survive restart. An overdue active sprint extends the series through today; completion extends through its actual finish date.

Canonical readers for dashboards are `getSprint(ctx,id)` and `getBurndown(ctx,id)`, exported by `packages/server/src/modules/work/sprints.js`; reuse them. Migration 251 creates `sprints(id,project_id,name,goal,start_date,end_date,status,started_at,completed_at,created_by,created_at,updated_at,result_json)`, `sprint_issues(sprint_id,issue_id,active,estimate,remaining,done,title,issue_key,added_at,removed_at)`, and `sprint_changes(id,sprint_id,issue_id,kind,at,scope_delta,remaining_delta,issue_delta,remaining_issue_delta)`. Sprint snapshots deliberately retain issue IDs without a live issue FK: deleting an issue records removal and preserves its historical title/key rather than deleting the evidence. Project deletion cascades sprint history. The issue event subscriber unregisters through ctx.cleanups.

`crew sprint help` prints all options. Commands include `list --project ID [--status STATE]`, `create --project ID --name NAME --start DATE --end DATE [--goal TEXT]`, `show ID`, `scope ID`, `update ID [--name NAME] [--goal TEXT] [--start DATE] [--end DATE]`, `add ID --issues ID,ID`, `remove ID --issue ID`, `start ID`, `complete ID [--carry-over ID]`, `burndown ID`, and `delete ID --yes`.

## Streaming attachments

`GET /issues/:issueId/attachments` lists metadata with cursor pagination and maxUploadBytes. `POST` to the same path streams raw bytes; pass `?name=filename` (URL encoded) and `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. Optional `X-Content-SHA256` is a 64-character hexadecimal expected digest. The server writes each chunk with backpressure, enforces the configured size even for chunked bodies, computes SHA-256, validates declared length/hash, and publishes metadata only after private bytes are complete. Permission `attachment:write` and live project state are checked before reading and again after upload before publication. Invalid/oversized/interrupted uploads remove temporary files and leave no attachment metadata. Size violations return 413 TOO_LARGE; field/hash errors return 422 VALIDATION.

`GET /attachments/:id` returns metadata. `GET /attachments/:id/download` streams exact bytes with Content-Length, X-Content-SHA256, an attachment disposition, and private no-store caching. Reads require project access. `DELETE /attachments/:id` requires attachment:write and removes bytes/metadata. Names cannot contain directory separators/control characters. Bytes live under CREW_DATA_DIR/attachments using opaque IDs, never supplied file names. Mutation events contain complete metadata; issue/project deletion reclaims associated blobs. Attachment rows retain explicit issue/project identifiers until those domain deletion events handle cleanup, avoiding FK removal before blob ownership is known.

`crew board attachments ISSUE`, `attach ISSUE --file PATH [--name NAME] [--sha256 HEX]`, `download ATTACHMENT --output PATH`, and `attachment-delete ATTACHMENT --yes` provide file operations. Upload uses a Node file stream. Download streams to a newly created private output file, verifies SHA-256 and size, and never replaces an existing output. Browser attachment panels support size prechecks, progress/cancel, hash details, download and deletion. After a connection uncertainty, check the list before deliberately trying another upload.

## CLI

`crew project list [--org ID] [--archived true|all] [--limit N] [--cursor CURSOR]`, `create --org ID --key KEY --name NAME [--description TEXT] [--workflow FILE]`, `show ID`, `update ID [--key KEY] [--name NAME] [--description TEXT] [--archived true|false]`, `archive ID`, `restore ID`, `delete ID --yes`, `workflow ID`, and `workflow-set ID --file FILE` use the same API and permissions. Workflow files contain a JSON status array. `crew board show PROJECT [--q TEXT] [--assignee ID]`, `board move ISSUE --status ID [--before ISSUE|--after ISSUE]`, and `board bulk PROJECT --issues ID,ID [--status ID] [--assignee ID|none] [--labels ID,ID|none] [--add-labels ID,ID] [--remove-labels ID,ID]` expose the board actions. All commands support global `--json`, `--url`, `--token` and `--config`.
